claim.quote: The excavation of the caverns that will house the gigantic particle detectors of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment in Lead, South Dakota is complete.

date.note: Date of the Fermilab press release announcing excavation completion.

name: Excavation of the DUNE far-site caverns completed at SURF
notes: Two related Fermilab announcements are cited: the 1 February 2024 completion-of-excavation press release (used for the result date) and the 15 August 2024 underground ribbon-cutting event marking the same milestone publicly; both describe the same excavation completion, not two separate results.
This atlas holds no DUNE physics result; this milestone and the ProtoDUNE-SP performance paper are the only DUNE entries in results/.

significance.note: A construction milestone, not a physics measurement; no significance applies.

summary.plain: Workers finished excavating the three caverns, about a mile underground in South Dakota, that will house DUNE's giant detectors. Fermilab said outfitting of the caverns would begin soon, followed by installation of the detectors.
summary.technical: Excavation of the three DUNE far-site caverns at the 4,850-foot level of SURF (two caverns, each more than 500 feet long and about seven stories tall, for the detector modules; a third for utilities), announced complete by Fermilab on 1 February 2024; the underground teams had been working there since 2021. A ribbon-cutting event marking the completion of excavation was held on 15 August 2024.

title: Excavation of colossal caverns for Fermilab's DUNE experiment completed
why_it_matters: The DUNE U.S. Project Director said completing the excavation prepares the project for installation of the detectors starting later in 2024; final outfitting of the caverns comes first.
